title: Auflauf von geriebener Gerste (Barley Soufflé)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, lemon, and raisins.

ingredients.name: a handful of raisins and citrons
ingredients.sourceText: a handful of raisins and citrons

steps: Mix 2 egg yolks with as much flour as they will absorb, ground as finely as possible
Cook this into a thick porridge in half a Maas of milk
Let it cool in a bowl
Stir 1/4 pound of butter until light
Take 4 Loth of sugar grated on half a lemon, 6 egg yolks, a handful of raisins and citrons, 2 Loth of cut citron peel, and the snow from the 6 egg whites, and add to the butter
Add the porridge to this mixture and blend everything well together
Butter a dish and fill the mass into it
Let the soufflé rise beautifully golden in the oven and sprinkle sugar on top

title: Augsburger Gansleberpastete (Augsburg Goose Liver Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with goose, lemon, and rusks.

ingredients.name: a handful of chopped and braised onions and parsley
ingredients.sourceText: a handful of chopped and braised onions and parsley

steps: Make a fine butter dough and line a melon mold with it.
Weigh 3 goose livers and cover them in a bowl.

Weigh 4 lemon peels, take one soaked and pressed rusk, the marrow from 4 lemons, a handful of chopped and braised onions and parsley, half a pound lean ham, salt, pepper, nutmeg, mace, 2 eggs and 1 egg yolk.
Mix everything together thoroughly.
Line the bottom of the mold with a handful of the mixture.
Cut 3 to 4 goose livers lengthwise and place on the mixture.
Add 1 spoonful of capers, place a mushroom on top, quarter pound cleaned truffles cut into leaves and crushed.
Add another handful of the mixture.
Cut 2 more goose livers lengthwise and place on top.
Add peeled olives, 1 spoonful capers, 4 to 6 mushrooms, truffles, and the mixture on top.
Place bacon slices on top and make a lid from the same dough.
Crimp with a pie crimper, brush the pie with eggs, and bake for 2 hours in the oven.
Cut an opening so steam can escape, cover again, and make an aspic.
Cook 3 to 4 blanched calf's feet with equal parts wine, vinegar, and water, celery, yellow carrots, 2 bay leaves, 2 large onions, whole cloves, mace, and whole pepper for 3 hours.
Pour through a hair sieve and let stand for a quarter hour.
Dip filter paper in it so the fat sticks to it.
Pour the jelly into a saucepan, avoiding the sediment.
Add a crushed egg, return to fire, and beat with a whisk until it boils.
Remove from fire, press in the juice from 1 lemon, cover with a lid with coals on top, and let stand for a quarter hour.
Pour the jelly through a felt hat and, when cold, pour it over the pie (must pour over 3 to 4 times).
Place the lid on top and set the pie in a cold place.

title: Ausgesteinte Kirschen (Pitted Cherries)
description: Prepared with cherries, sugar, and water.
steps: Pit 2 pounds of beautiful cherries, taking care not to lose too much juice
For 2 pounds of cherries, use 1½ pounds of sugar and cook it in a brass pan or saucepan with half a bottle's measure of water until the sugar spins thick threads
Add the cherries along with some whole cinnamon and cook as long as it takes for hard-boiled eggs
Lift out the cherries with a skimming spoon
Cook the syrup until it rises above the pan
Place the cherries in their designated dish and pour the syrup, after it has been well reduced, over them
Let cool and store like other preserved sugar items; they will keep for 2 years

title: Backobst (Dried Fruit Compote)
description: Prepared with dried fruit, potato flour, and sugar.
steps: Wash the dry fruit preferably the evening before use and place it in an earthen pot with 3/8 liter fresh water to soak.

The next morning, without changing the water, bring the dried fruit to a boil in the same pot with orange peel, cinnamon and half the sugar, then cover, push back and simmer very slowly for 2-3 hours to soften, without stirring; only shake the pot occasionally. If necessary, add some water so that there is plenty of broth. Lift out the fruit, mix the remaining sugar with the juice, cook this down to 1/8 liter and mix with potato flour dissolved in water; arrange the fruit with the sauce poured over it.

title: Baierische Dampfnudeln (Bavarian Steamed Noodles)
description: Prepared with beer, flour, and milk.
steps: In a bowl make a small dough with {{source-0}}, 3 spoonfuls beer yeast and 1 Schoppen lukewarm milk, let it rise well in gentle warmth.
Cut quarter pound butter to it, along with 2 whole eggs and yolks, work the dough until it throws bubbles.
Let it rise in the warmth, and when it is quite ripe, place cloth on a noodle board, sprinkle flour on it, set the noodles, as large as a hen's egg, on it and let them rise a little more.
Let quarter pound butter melt in a suitable dish, but do not let it become hot.
Pour approximately 1 Schoppen milk to it, 1 Loth pounded sugar.
Set the steamed noodles in the dish and a cover with weak coals on top.
Place the dish on a trivet, put a little coals under it and let it cook through.

title: Baumnüsse (Candied Walnuts)
description: Prepared with walnuts, cherry, and sugar.
steps: Break the walnuts around Saint John's Day when they are still soft and milky
Cut a little off the top and bottom
Pierce 2 to 3 holes with a stick on each side
Lay them in fresh spring water for 8 days
Cook them in a brass pan for a quarter hour in water
Pour off the water, add fresh water, and repeat this three times
Test the nuts with a small stick to see if they are soft; if not, cook them once more
When soft, place them in cold water
Drain the water 3 times
Lay them on a hair sieve and let them dry
Lard the nuts with cinnamon and cloves
Lay them in a sugar jar
For 50 nuts, take 1-1/2 pounds sugar
Clarify this in a brass pan with cinnamon water until it spins a thick thread
Pour the clarified sugar over the nuts
Let them stand for 2 days
On the third day, pour off the sugar again
Let it boil once more, add another piece of sugar
Pour it over the nuts again and repeat this 3 to 4 times
The last time let the nuts cook along with it for a while
Preserve them well in a glass
Lay paper soaked in cherry spirits on top
Store in a dry place

description: Prepared with veal, onion, and turnips.
steps: Cut veal into small pieces and braise it gently in a saucepan with a piece of butter, onion, yellow turnips, and celery.
Add 3 handfuls of flour and braise together again.
Press everything through a sieve.
Beat 4 eggs into it.
Stir it together well with salt and nutmeg in a bowl.
Butter a long mold and fill it with the mixture.
Poach it in a water bath.
Cut or shape small cakes from it, dip them in eggs and grated bread, and fry them in hot lard.

title: Beefsteak (Beef Steak)
description: Prepared with onion, gravy, and salt.
steps: Cut a piece of loin roast into small pieces, but not as thick as English beefsteaks
Beat them flat with your hand
Rub them with salt and pepper
Pour fine oil into a vessel and turn the beefsteaks in it
Place them in a pan with a piece of butter
Add a weighed onion
Let them fry golden brown
Arrange the whole on a plate

title: Bierfisch (Beer Fish)
description: Prepared with fish, beer, and fat.
steps: Cut the prepared fish into hand-width pieces, then clean them so that the pieces remain round and whole and do not fall apart at the belly during cooking
Wash the pieces clean and quickly, dry them and salt with 10 g salt
Clean, wash and cut the soup greens into small strips
Peel the onions and cut into slices
Break up the bread crust
Render the fat, pour in the flour and stir well
Pour the beer over it, add the spices and let everything cook covered until the soup greens are soft
Season the sauce with syrup and 5 g salt
Place the fish in the boiling sauce, in which it must slowly cook until done
To check if the fish is done, pull out a fin; if it comes off easily without being bloody, the fish is done
Serve with the sauce in a bowl
Instead of syrup, grated gingerbread can be used, but then use less flour
Cook roe separately in boiling salt water and arrange on top

title: Birnen in Essig (Pears in Vinegar)
description: Prepared with pears, wine, and sugar.

ingredients.name: wine vinegar, not too sharp
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 l wine vinegar, not too sharp

steps: Preparation: Prepare smaller pears by peeling them whole, larger pears by halving them and carefully coring the seed cavity, or table pears by peeling and cutting into quarters. While preparing the pears, dissolve {{source-1}} in vinegar and skim.
Preparation: Cook the spices (in a muslin bag) with the vinegar and sugar. Blanch the pears in water, sugar and vinegar, then lay them drained into the sugar vinegar and cook them until soft.

Fill the pears into glasses or pots and reduce the sugar vinegar until it falls in broad drops from the spoon. After it cools, pour it over the pears (leaving the spices behind) and seal the containers as directed.
After a few days, pour the pears onto a colander, cook the thinned vinegar down to the second degree, and after it cools, pour it over the pears returned to the containers.
If the liquid is still thinned by the juice from the pears, it must be reduced again; if it has reduced too much, sugar and vinegar must be added.

title: Blutreinigende Kräutermilch für Kinder (Blood-Purifying Herb Milk for Children)
description: Prepared with milk and salt.

ingredients.name: Edelleber-, Erdbeeren-, Körbel-, Löffel-, Pfennig- und Sternleberkraut
ingredients.sourceText: Edelleber-, Erdbeeren-, Körbel-, Löffel-, Pfennig- und Sternleberkraut

steps: Pick the herbs very clean without washing them
Weigh one handful of each herb
Chop the herbs as finely as possible
Add one knife-tip full of salt
Press the juice into a glazed pot
Leave it in the cellar overnight
In the morning, heat one Maas of milk
Pour 3 to 4 spoonfuls of the juice into the hot milk
Give it to the child to drink (a 10-year-old child gets one whole Schoppen, a 5-year-old gets half a Schoppen)
Continue this cure for 14 days
Make the juice fresh twice a week
Optionally add a small piece of butter and an egg yolk

title: Boeuf à la Mode (Beef à la Mode)
description: Prepared with beef, vinegar, and wine.

ingredients.name: beef from the hind quarter or a good tail piece
ingredients.sourceText: beef from the hind quarter or a good tail piece

steps: Pound the beef until tender and place in a dish
Pour equal parts vinegar and wine as desired
Cut all sorts of roots and add lemons, bay leaves, whole pepper, and cloves
Cover the meat tightly and let it stand 2 to 3 days, turning it daily
On the day of cooking, put everything together in a casserole
Cut the crust from black bread and add it, pour in 1 spoonful of meat broth or water
Cover tightly and cook until soft in the oven or over coals
Remove the meat, press everything through a hair sieve, remove the fat
Put the sauce back in the casserole, add the meat, and let it cook together for another half hour
Add the zest and juice of half a lemon and a knife point of mace
If the sauce is not thick enough, soak a piece of brown gingerbread in a little meat broth until soft and stir it into the sauce

title: Bohnen (Preserved Beans)
description: Prepared with beans, grape, and salt.
steps: Remove the strings from the beans and cut them as desired, large or small
Boil water in a kettle, salt it well and add the beans
Cook for 4 minutes, quickly remove them and place in cold water for a quarter hour
Place in a basket to drain well and dry on a noodle board

Preserve in a well-pitched small barrel as follows: lay grape leaves on the bottom, some coarsely pounded pepper and salt, then a layer of beans, pepper and salt on top, then again beans, continuing until the barrel is full
Press the beans down firmly by hand and cover the top of the barrel again with grape leaves

description: Prepared with beans and salt.
steps: Pick snap beans and string beans while they are still tender and not tough or stringy. Remove the strings, cut them finely or break them, and immediately mix with salt.

Spread a layer of salt on the bottom of a large tall stoneware or Bunzlau pot, then layer the salted beans without any other additions and pack them down firmly with a wooden stirring stick, which is important for proper preservation.

Lay a piece of clean old linen cloth on top, which prevents mold formation and can later be easily washed if necessary. Then place a porcelain lid or similar on top, which is weighted down with a clean field stone. The pot of beans can be stored in any place that is not too warm.

Alternatively: Pack them layer by layer with salt in glasses or pots. Lay a suitable small board on top, weighted down with a stone. As soon as brine has formed, remove the stone and board, pour melted warm fat over the brine, and tie up the pot. Larger quantities, well mixed with salt, can be placed in a stone pot under the weight of a field stone lying on a clean cloth and used as needed. The cloth should be washed frequently.

title: Bohnen, Süss-Saure (Sweet and Sour Beans)
description: Prepared with white beans, bacon, and onion.
steps: Prepare: Soak the beans the evening before; dice the bacon and onion; prepare {{source-5}} for the sauce and season with syrup, vinegar, pepper and salt.

Cook the beans with 1 pinch salt and cold, soft water, blanch, drain and cook covered slowly and tender with 1-1/2 liters water and 8 g salt. Meanwhile, fry the bacon cubes in an earthenware pot, remove the cracklings and keep them warm, let the sugar brown in the fat, add the diced onions to the fat and let them brown, as well as the flour. Add the liquid slowly with stirring and it must cook thick with the brown flour. Drain the tender beans, mix with the finished sauce, taste again, pour into a bowl, sprinkle the cracklings over and serve.

title: Bohnen-, Linsen- oder Erbsensuppe (Bean, Lentil or Pea Soup)
description: A soup made with beans or lentils or peas, celery, and beef.

ingredients.name: chopped celery greens or leek
ingredients.sourceText: 1 teaspoon chopped celery greens or leek

steps: Soak the beans, lentils or peas the evening before according to instructions.

Place the legumes in 1 l cold water with soda, heat and drain. Add beef, celery cubes, salt and 1 l water to the legumes, seal the pot tightly and cook the contents slowly for 2 hours. In a small bowl, sweat the onions, chopped greens and flour, add a few spoonfuls of soup and cook the flour mixture with the entire dish, which you season with pepper.
Serve the meat separately.

title: Bohnensalat (Bean Salad)
description: A salad made with beans, onions, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: (1-1/2 pounds) snap beans or wax beans
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 kg (1-1/2 pounds) snap beans or wax beans

steps: Prepare: Remove the beans, break them, wash them. Chop the parsley, grate the onion.

Cook the beans in plenty of boiling salt water; once they feel very tender, run them under cold water on a sieve. After draining well, mix them with oil, a little broth or hot water and salt, and mix with a spoon; gradually add onions, pepper and vinegar and mix carefully until all liquid is absorbed; then taste the beans carefully, sprinkle chopped parsley or chives over them and arrange the salad in a mound.

title: Bouillon (Beef Broth)
description: A soup made with beef, veal bones, and hen.
steps: Put the beef, veal bones, and hen together in a three-measure pot with cold water and some salt
Bring to a boil and skim off the foam diligently
Add the scraped and cut celery roots, bay leaves, yellow carrots, leek, parsley root, and the onion studded with cloves
Let it cook over gentle heat until the meat is tender
Remove the meat, pour the broth through a hair sieve, skim off the fat, and set it in a cool place
This bouillon is used for all white sauces

title: Bouletten (German Meatballs)
description: Prepared with meat, breadcrumbs, and fat or margarine.
steps: Rub the roll into crumbs, break it up, put it in a pot and pour {{source-9}} over it. Finely chop the cooked lean meat and cracklings on a wooden board with a mincing knife.
In a bowl, mix the roll pressed out in a clean cloth or sieve with egg, salt, pepper and grated onion, mix thoroughly with the minced mixture and adjust the seasoning.

Heat fat or margarine in a pan until smoking, form 4 equal sized balls from the meat mixture, flatten them, press diagonal squares into them with the back of a knife, roll them in grated breadcrumbs, slowly fry them for 6 minutes on both sides in smoking fat until they have a nice color and serve them poured over with the fat.

title: Bozener Hutzelnbrod (Bolzano Fruit Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with medlars, raisins, and wine.

ingredients.name: blanched and finely cut almonds
ingredients.sourceText: 1 pound blanched and finely cut almonds

ingredients.name: citron and bitter orange peel
ingredients.sourceText: 1 pound citron and bitter orange peel

steps: Cook medlars until very soft and cut into small pieces
Remove pits and stems
Mix together raisins, wine grapes, plums, figs, almonds, spices, citron, and orange peel thoroughly
Place flour on a pastry board and make a firm dough with water
Roll out very thick as a knife back
Spread the fruit mixture inside
Form into a round loaf no more than 4 fingers high
Press lightly and place in the oven
Bake until golden
For the icing: stir egg whites, finely ground sugar, and lemon juice into a thick icing
Coat the bread thickly with the icing
Garnish with candied fruits as desired

title: Braten von Schwarzwildbret (Roast Wild Boar)
description: Prepared with wine, vinegar, and bacon.
steps: Remove the skin from the leg of young wild boar and cut the lower bone so that the hooves and skin remain attached.
Place it in a mixture of equal parts wine and vinegar with all sorts of roots, herbs, and coarsely crushed spices, turning it often.
On the day it is to be served, remove it from the marinade.
Make holes in the bottom with a knife and insert a piece of bacon into each hole.
Roast it in a casserole in the oven until beautifully golden, along with the marinade.
Finely chop one tablespoon of capers, one smoked herring, one onion, and the zest of half a lemon.
Mix together two egg whites, a knife-point of cinnamon, the same amount of mace, and the juice of half a lemon in a bowl.
When the leg is tender, spread this mixture on top of it to the thickness of a knife-back.
Roast it in the oven until golden, basting it 2 to 3 times with the fat.
Arrange the roast on a plate, garnish with lemons, place the shank with hooves on top, and serve the jus strained through a fine sieve separately.

title: Bratwurst (Bratwurst Sausage)
description: Prepared with salt and water.
steps: Wash the bratwurst and divide it into two equal pieces.
If the bratwurst is fatty enough, place it in the pan without additional fat, pour one spoon of water over it, and fry the sausage under frequent turning in its own fat to a nice color.
Place the finished sausage on a plate and pour the available fat over it.

If a vegetable with sauce is added, this is sufficient. Otherwise, add to the fat in the pan 10 g flour, 1 pinch pepper and salt, make a brown roux from it, add 1/4 liter broth or wheat beer while stirring, color the sauce with a drop of brown sugar and adjust the seasoning.
Alternatively, prepare the sauce first and let the sausage simmer in it for 1/2 hour.

title: Braune Jussuppe (Brown Meat Broth Soup)
description: A soup made with meat, onions, and turnips.

ingredients.name: Butter the size of an egg (for dumplings)
ingredients.sourceText: Butter the size of an egg (for dumplings)

steps: Place a piece of butter, cut onions and yellow turnips in a casserole
Cut 3 pounds of lean beef into small pieces and brown them nicely in the casserole
Add a head of white cabbage cut up
Pour a ladle full of water over it
When it is brown, cover the casserole for a little while
Pour in meat broth and let it cook 2 to 3 hours
Pass it through a hair sieve into another casserole and let it come to a boil
For the fried peas: bring half a Maas water to a boil in a brass pan with a piece of butter the size of a hen's egg
Stir in fine flour until it becomes a thick paste
Transfer to a bowl and beat in 5 to 6 eggs
Add 2 knife points of salt
Force this dough through a sparrow sieve into hot lard and fry the peas until nicely yellow

title: Brieschen (Calf Sweetbreads)
description: Prepared with calf sweetbreads, onion, and lemon.

Put them in cold water and bring to a boil
Remove them and pass through cold water again
Remove the membrane and lard them nicely
Put a piece of butter in a casserole, lay the sweetbreads with sliced onion, lemon, bay leaf, and mace in the butter
Pour a little meat broth over them and braise covered for half an hour
Sprinkle three finger widths of flour over the sweetbreads, turn them over, pour a little cold water over, fill with meat broth, and let everything cook together for a quarter hour
When serving, lay the sweetbreads on a plate, strain the sauce through a fine sieve over them, and salt to taste

Cook another quarter hour in steam so that the fat remains on top
Preserve in the cellar

title: Brühsuppe mit Nudeln, Griess oder Einlauf und Rindfleisch (Broth Soup with Noodles, Semolina or Egg Drop and Beef)

ingredients.name: 1 grated carrot or peel of a red onion
ingredients.sourceText: 1 grated carrot or peel of a red onion

steps: Place the water with salt and any available cleaned bones on the stove covered; clean, wash and cut the soup vegetables; wash and pound the beef.

Once the water with the bones boils, add the meat; after it has cooked with the scum for some time, remove the scum, add the cut soup vegetables, and to color the broth a grated carrot or raw onion peel, seal the pot tightly and let the meat simmer slowly for 2-2½ hours. When the meat is tender, remove it and keep it warm, season the broth, remove the bones, skim the fat from the broth and add noodles, semolina or egg drop, cook the soup for another 10 minutes and serve soup and meat.

title: Böhmische Kolatschen (Bohemian Kolaches)
description: Prepared with beer, egg yolks, and apricot jam.
steps: Make a starter dough from flour, yeast, and warm milk in a bowl
Let it rise well in gentle warmth
Work in egg yolks and ground sugar by hand
Roll out on a pastry board
Distribute 12 loth butter on the dough and fold it over

Press a depression with an egg

Top with a little egg white snow
Sprinkle with sugar and vanilla
Bake for half an hour, not too hot

title: Consommé (Concentrated Meat Broth)
description: A soup made with beef, veal bones, and veal.
steps: Chop all the meat and bones into pieces and put in a large kettle
Pour enough water over it so it rises 3 fingers above the contents
Let it cook for 10 to 12 hours, skimming diligently
Do not salt it; use few herbs and roots to prevent souring
Refill with water often during cooking
Let it reduce to half its volume, then strain through a hair sieve
Let it stand overnight if time permits
The next day, remove the fat from the top and put the remainder in a casserole
Let it cook until a sample on a plate remains in drops
Skim continuously during cooking
Pour through linen into a flat dish and cut into small tablets like chocolate when firm
It is especially good for poultry and for glazing, and can be used to prepare the strongest meat broths and cleanest soups

Using a spoon, make 2 lattices of the syrup over the quenelles

title: Cured Meat (Pökelfleisch)
description: Prepared with beef or brisket, saltpeter, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: Beef from the brisket or tail piece
ingredients.sourceText: Beef from the brisket or tail piece

steps: Choose a piece of beef from the brisket for serving warm, or from the tail for serving cold.
Rub the meat well with 2 loth of saltpeter.
Lay it in a stone pot or tub.
Crush the following herbs: tarragon, thyme, basil, bay leaves, lemon balm, celery herb, rosemary, marjoram, cloves, pepper, nutmeg, and juniper berries, and add all to the meat.
Cover it and place it in the cellar for 2 to 3 days.
On the fourth day, cook the spices in a pan with 1 pound of salt and 1½ maas of water until no salt is visible.
Let it cool completely.
Pour it again over the meat, cover it firmly, lay 2 stones on top.
Let it stand for 3 days, turn it on the third day, add the pickle brine again, and continue this for 3 to 4 weeks.
To cook, place it in a not very large pot with water; it must not be salted.
Serve it warm with horseradish; it is also very good with sauerkraut, winter cabbage, and beans.

title: Eier in brauner Sauce (Eggs in Brown Sauce)
description: A sauce made with eggs, lard, and bread.
steps: Fry as many eggs as needed in hot lard, but keep the yolk soft
For the sauce: take a handful of grated black bread and 2 loth brown gingerbread together in a casserole
Pour in a glass of wine, half a glass of vinegar, a ladle-full of meat broth or water on fasting days
Add the juice of half a lemon, salt, pepper, and nutmeg
Let it boil together for a quarter hour
Strain through a hair sieve
Place the eggs on a plate, pour the sauce over them, and let everything become hot together again

title: Eiercrêmetorte (Egg Cream Torte)
description: A cake made with cream, egg yolks, and egg whites.

ingredients.name: butter and sugar for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: butter and sugar for the pan

steps: Stir {{source-0}} with 20 egg yolks and the snow of 16 egg whites until the mass is thick
Add the grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
Mix in 16 loth starch flour
Brush a plafond 3 fingers high and not very wide with butter, sprinkle with sugar, and bake the torte in it
For the cream: dissolve 1-1/2 loth fish glue in 1 schoppen water
Pour the water through a hair sieve
Grate the zest of 1 orange with 6 loth sugar
Pour the fish glue water into a brass pan
Take the sugar, 1 schoppen sweet cream, juice of 2 oranges, and 6 egg yolks
Cook everything on the fire into a cream
Pour it through a hair sieve into a porcelain bowl and let it cool
Beat 1 schoppen sweet cream in a bowl like snow
Let it drain in a hair sieve and mix it into the cold cream
Place the torte on a plate and remove the lid from the top
Cut a 2-inch deep opening into the torte and hollow it out
Pour the cream into it
Replace the lid
Make a lemon or chocolate icing on the lid as has been described before
Decorate the torte with citron peel and preserved fruits

title: Eierkuchen (Pancake)
description: Prepared with skim milk, fat, and egg.
steps: Crack the egg, separating yolk and white into different pots
Beat the yolk with milk and salt, then gradually stir it into the center of the flour along with the baking powder
Beat the egg white until stiff and slowly fold into the mixture, which should not sit
Wipe a handled frying pan dry with paper
Heat 1 spoon of fat in the pan until hot
Slowly pour in the batter and distribute evenly by moving the pan back and forth

Brown the first side of the pancake nicely over frequent shaking, slide it onto a lid, add about 10 g fat to the unbaked side, cover the pan with the lid, flip, let the pancake steam covered for a few moments, then remove the lid
The cake should have risen nicely; bake to a nice color, serve, and sprinkle with sugar
Pancakes should not sit; if necessary, keep them only on a pot of hot water

title: Ein altes Weib (An Old Woman)
description: Prepared with bread, lard, and red wine.
steps: Heat 1 schoppen water and butter the size of a hen's egg in a brass pan.
Stir in fine flour until very thick, cook until the batter pulls away from the pan, and smooth it with 3 eggs (the batter must be such that it runs off a spoon).
Cut a small piece of white bread, shape it round, dip it in the batter and fry golden in a deep pan with hot lard.
Stick it on a strong fork, turn it in the batter again, and repeat this 12 to 15 times.
Once the bread is large enough, place it on bread slices to drain well.
Make an English sauce: stir 1 small cooking spoon flour with cold water, add 1 schoppen red wine, sugar to taste, a knife-tip of ground cinnamon, and {{source-10}}, and bring to a boil.
In a small pan, place a piece of sugar, add 1 tablespoon water, cook until it spins threads, add to the sauce, and bring everything to a boil once more.
Place the old woman on the plate and pour the sauce over her.

ingredients.sourceText: Piece of loin roast with fat from a fat ox slaughtered 8 days prior

steps: Season a piece of loin roast with fat with salt and pepper
Put it on a spit and wrap it double with 4 sheets of paper
Roast it slowly over weak fire for 4 hours, basting constantly with pure clear butter

Leave the roast on the fire and baste several more times with melted pure butter
Place it on the platter, strain the jus through a sieve, remove the fat, and pour the jus over the roast

For the lemon sauce: rub 2 lemons over sugar, mix with a cooking spoon of flour and cold water, add 1 pint of wine, the lemon sugar, and the juice, and pour this sauce over the pudding.

title: Englischer Pudding anderer Art (English Pudding Another Way)
description: A pudding made with beef, lemon, and citron.
steps: Chop the beef kidney fat very finely.
Rub 20 loth flour with the hand and mix into the chopped fat.
Add 8 loth finely pounded sugar, zest of half a lemon grated on the grater, 8 loth citron and orange peel finely chopped, 8 loth small raisins, 8 loth large raisins washed clean.
Beat 4 whole eggs and mix everything with a cooking spoon together like a sparrow dough.
Tie the mass firmly in a cloth dipped in cold water and put it in boiling water.
Cook for three hours.
Serve with flaming Arak or any desired sauce.

title: Estragonessig auf französische Art (Tarragon Vinegar, French Style)
description: Prepared with tarragon, wine, and shallot.

ingredients.name: a strong handful of tender tarragon leaves
ingredients.sourceText: a strong handful of tender tarragon leaves

steps: Take a strong handful of tender tarragon leaves and pour good wine vinegar over them together with 6 pieces pimpernelle, 6 shallot onions, 8 cloves, 8 white peppercorns, a piece of whole ginger, a piece of whole cinnamon and some lemon in a clean container
Bind the container firmly shut
Set it in the sun for 14 days or 3 weeks, or otherwise in a warm place
After 3 weeks the vinegar is excellently good
Fill it into bottles, seal these firmly and the vinegar can be used for sauces and for salad

title: Farcirte Aepfel (Stuffed Apples)
description: Prepared with apples, wine, and citron.
steps: Peel and halve the apples, remove the cores, and hollow them out slightly without making holes
Cook the apples in 1 schoppen wine, 1 schoppen water, and 10 loth sugar until soft
Drain on a hair sieve
Press the yolks of 4 hard-boiled eggs through a hair sieve
Finely weigh 1 loth candied citron and 1 loth blanched almonds
Mix them with the eggs and 1 loth sugar
Place the apples on a plate with the openings facing up
Fill half of each apple with the egg mixture and cover with the other half
Cook 2 spoonfuls raspberry or currant juice with the syrup until it bubbles
Pour the syrup over the apples to give them a nice glaze

title: Farcirte Eier (Stuffed Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, bread, and currants.
steps: Boil eggs hard, peel them, and place them in cold water.
Cut them lengthwise in half and carefully remove the yolk.
Cut the hard crust from white bread, soak it in water, and press it firmly out.
Let a piece of butter melt in a casserole, add the bread and hard-boiled egg yolks, along with a handful of cleaned small currants.
Cook this all together over the fire, beat in one egg, 2 spoonfuls of sour cream, salt and nutmeg.
Stir it once more over the fire and fill the hard-boiled egg whites with this mixture.
Beat 3 egg yolks in half a pint of sweet cream on the plate intended for serving, pour it over the eggs, and let them become nicely golden in a baking oven.
Beat 3 egg yolks in a brass pan, add a small piece of butter and half a pint of sweet cream, let this come together over the fire, and pour the sauce over the eggs.

title: Farcirte Feldhühner (Stuffed Partridge)
description: Prepared with partridges, bacon, and onions.
steps: Pluck and singe one partridge, cut off the head (unplucked), remove the crop, split the back, and remove the breast so all meat remains attached to the skin.
Carefully remove all bones from the body (keeping only the leg bone).
Cut the feet at the second joint.
From a second partridge, remove all meat and mince finely with {{source-1}}, adding onions and lemons.
Pound in a mortar or on a rubbing stone until very fine.
Add truffles, salt, and mace.
Mix in a bowl with 1 egg.
Add grated white bread (for 1 kreuzer) that has been soaked in milk and firmly pressed out, and mix well again.
Fill the first bird with this mixture.
Sew the back closed.
Bind with bacon.
In a casserole with a piece of fat, onions, juniper berries, and yellow turnips, braise slowly and beautifully.
Serve hot or cold, best with mayonnaise sauce.

title: Farcirter Hecht (Stuffed Pike)
description: Prepared with pike, pork fat, and bacon.
steps: Clean the pike carefully, cut out the gills, make a careful cut at the opening below, and cut the skin on the back; make a stitch at the fins but not completely through, then remove the skin

Lard the pike nicely with a mixture made from {{source-1}}, {{source-2}}, 4 anchovies, bread that has been soaked in milk and squeezed out and finely ground, salt, nutmeg, pepper, and finely chopped steamed onions, all mixed together with 2 eggs and thoroughly pounded in a mortar
Fill the pike with this mixture and sew it shut
Place it in a roasting pan with a rack at the bottom, add sliced onions, 1 bay leaf, lemons, and a little meat broth
Roast in the oven until golden, frequently basting with hot butter
When serving, let consommé melt over it, coat the pike with it, and pour the sauce through a hair sieve over it

title: Farcirter Kapaun auf russische Art (Stuffed Capon Russian Style)
description: Prepared with fat, ham, and cream.
steps: Pierce the capon and let it bleed thoroughly.
Pluck it while warm, carefully to avoid holes.
Singe off remaining hairs over a flame.
Remove innards carefully, drawing out the crop with the intestines from below, but leave the heart and lungs.
Loosen the breast, back, and thighs as you would a young dove.
Prepare the filling: mince the lean ham very finely, add three eggs, pour in one schoppen sweet cream, add one grated nutmeg.
Fill a syringe with a tube the thickness of a small finger with this mixture.
Inject and fill the capon with the mass.
Sew the opening closed again.
Place the head with beak on the breast, arrange the feet nicely, place a lemon wheel on the breast.
Wrap in a sheet of paper thickly brushed with butter.
Roast slowly in a braising pan, basting frequently.
Can be served as a roast or ragout. For ragout, prepare sauce: melt a piece of butter in a casserole and braise finely cut onions and a small piece of sugar for a good quarter hour.
Sprinkle in one cooking spoon of flour, mix, add one large spoon of meat broth and one glass of wine.
Let simmer for half an hour.
Force the sauce through a hair sieve back into the casserole.
Add the yolk and marrow of one finely minced lemon.
Let come to a boil once more and rub in one nutmeg.
When ready to serve, place the capon carefully on a platter and pour the sauce directly onto the platter, not over the capon.

title: Feldhühner in Salmisauce (Partridges in Salmi Sauce)
description: A sauce made with partridges, onion, and lemon.
steps: Clean and pluck the partridges, singe them, cut off the wings at the second joint and remove the heads and innards.
If the partridges are fresh, do not wash them but rub them inside with salt and pepper.
Insert an onion studded with cloves and a piece of lemon into the opening.
Wrap the partridges with bacon and place them in a casserole with chopped onion, carrots, bay leaves, juniper berries, a piece of fat, and the heads, wings, stomach and liver.
Cover the casserole and let it brown well.
When cooked, place the partridges on a platter to keep warm.
Remove the other ingredients from the casserole and pound them finely in a mortar.
Pour the pounded mixture back into the casserole.
Add a bread crust fried in lard.
Pour in a schoppen of red wine and a spoonful of jus.
Let it boil for a quarter hour, strain through a fine sieve and pour back into the casserole.
Add the partridges and chopped lemon, cloves, nutmeg, pepper and salt to taste.

title: Feldhühnerpastete (Partridge Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with partridges, pork, and bread.
steps: Cut the breasts from 6 partridges and remove bones from 2 breasts
Pound the meat finely in a mortar
Rub half a pound pork sausage meat, a soaked and firmly pressed out Kreuzerbrod and 2 eggs on a grater until foamy
Put the grated mixture in a bowl
Pound 3 Loth cleaned anchovies with 3 Loth butter, the minced zest of 1 lemon, salt, pepper, nutmeg and mace and add it
Lard 4 chicken breasts and the legs, place them with cut bacon, butter, onions, juniper berries, carrots and celery in a casserole
Cover and braise them for half an hour
Chop the bodies of the partridges together and braise them as well
Line a melon mold with butter pastry
Place half of the stirred mass in it
Place the breasts and legs on top
Place a spoonful of capers and 2 to 3 cleaned truffles over it
Cover with the other half of the stirred mixture
Pour the fat in which they were braised over it
Make a lid of butter pastry on top, brush it with egg, pinch it well together and bake the pastry in the oven

title: Filets von jungen Hühnern mit süßem Rahm (Fillets of Young Hens with Sweet Cream)
description: Prepared with hens, béchamel, and veal.
steps: Roast the young hens half-done.
When cold, remove the skin.
Cut the white meat into fine fillets and cook with Béchamel sauce and some glace.
For the Béchamel: cut one pound of veal shank into small pieces.
In a covered casserole, gently braise the veal with one pound of butter, onions and parsley.
Sprinkle two handfuls of flour over it, stir a few times, cover and braise for a few more minutes.
Pass everything through a fine sieve using a vegetable mill.
Place a piece of butter and the Béchamel in a casserole.
Stir in 3 egg yolks, salt and nutmeg, and stir several times.
Pour the Béchamel onto the serving platter.
Place the young hens on top and squeeze the juice of half a lemon over them.

description: Prepared with fish, onion, and lemon.
steps: Make forcemeat from inferior fish and lay it in milk for half an hour

Do not let them stand long or they will become tough

title: Fischotter (Otter Fish Stew)
description: Prepared with fish, onions, and lemon.
steps: Skin the otter fish and cut into pieces
Soak in cold water for 5 to 6 days, changing the water daily
On the sixth day, remove and soak for 2 days in good wine with onions, cloves, mace, lemon, and various herbs and spices
Place with a bottle of Port or stone wine over the fire and let simmer for one hour
For the truffle sauce: line a casserole thickly with onions
Cook a piece of fat and 1-1/2 pounds of finely cut veal until golden
Add half a ladle of the stock in which the otter was cooked, bread crust, and some flour
Cook together and strain through a fine sieve
Weigh 2 to 3 truffels with their rough skin removed, with the citron yellow and juice
Add a pinch of nutmace, some white pepper, and 3 cubeb kernels
Place the otter fish in the sauce
Simmer for a while and add sliced mushrooms and truffles
Cook everything a bit longer

description: A pudding made with fish, onion, and lemon.
steps: Mince the onion and steam it in 1/2 quarter pound butter
Mix the fish forcemeat, soaked roll, steamed onion and 3 eggs together for a quarter hour

Steam the minced thymus with a piece of butter in a casserole
Sprinkle half a cooking spoon of flour over it
Stir smooth with cold water
Bring to a boil with one spoonful of good meat broth
Add salt and juice of half a lemon
Place the pudding on a plate and pour the sauce over it

steps: Fish broth or cooking water from good fresh fish is well suited for this soup. description: Prepared with fish, onions, and lemons.
steps: Scale and clean the fish, cutting the skin open along the back and peeling it off
Scrape the flesh from the bones and soak it for half an hour in milk to make it white

Add 2 to 3 eggs and stir for another quarter hour
Add the braised vegetables with salt and nutmeg
Press the mass into casings and place the sausages in warm water
Fry them on a grill or in a pan

title: Fleischhache mit Reis (Meat and Rice Hash)
description: Prepared with meat, rice, and broth.
steps: Prepare a rice porridge from washed, blanched rice and rich meat broth (or 1 teaspoon fat and meat extract broth), 1 onion which is cooked whole and later removed, the necessary salt, and finally the grated cheese.
Let the coarsely chopped meat, to which one can also use cooked ham or cured meat, simmer for a few minutes in hot brown margarine along with {{source-4}}, the pepper, and flour.
Combine the meat and rice.

Alternatively: Layer rice and meat, each prepared separately, in alternating layers so that rice forms the top layer on a butter-brushed dish from which the dish can be brought both to the oven and to table, brush one beaten egg over it, sprinkle the surface with grated cheese, and let the hash brown in the oven.

Alternatively: Press both in layers into a well-buttered mold dusted with breadcrumbs and bring the dish turned out, with a piquant brown or Dutch sauce to table. The meat can also be cut into thin slices, sprinkled with margarine pieces and grated cheese, and prepared with the rice according to the various instructions above. (Requires more fat and cheese.)

title: Fleischklösse, Gebratene (Fried Meat Balls)
description: Prepared with beef, pork, and bread.

ingredients.name: fat or margarine for frying
ingredients.sourceText: 25 g fat or margarine for frying

steps: Peel the bread roll, cut it into pieces, and soak it.

Mix beef, pork, egg, squeezed-out bread roll, pepper, salt, and onion thoroughly together in a bowl; form this mixture into 4 uniform balls, press them smooth, roll them in grated bread roll, and fry them in steaming fat for 7 minutes slowly with frequent turning.

Alternatively, form the entire mixture into an oblong shape and fry it in a pan with 1 tablespoon fat for 1/2 hour under frequent basting; gradually pour a few spoons of water under the roast and thicken the sauce after removing it with 3 g potato flour mixed in 2 tablespoons water.

Alternatively (Fleischpudding): In a greased, breadcrumb-lined sealed mold, the well-pressed mixture is cooked for 1 1/2 hours in a water bath or in a pressure cooker, turned out, and served with sauce of choice. The frying fat is then omitted.

description: A salad made with meat, broth, and mustard.
steps: Cut the meat into cubes or small fillets. Slice the gherkin.
Mix the meat with the broth and then with mustard, onions, vinegar, and herbs. Season with pepper, salt, and optionally 4 drops of Maggi seasoning. Cover and let stand for 1-2 hours.

This salad can be refined by using pearl onions, capers, etc. as ingredients. Fish or poultry salad are prepared the same way, only the pieces are irregular and of arbitrary size.

title: Forellen mit saurer Sulz (Trout in Sour Jelly)
description: Prepared with trout, calf's feet, and isinglass.
steps: Boil the trout blue and place on a dish, cover tightly so the blue color does not fade
Chop 2 cleaned calf's feet together with 1 Loth isinglass, add fish broth so it makes 1-1.5 Maas
Cook for 2 to 3 hours, strain the jelly through a fine sieve and let it stand in a bowl for a quarter hour so the sediment remains on the bottom
Draw a sheet of blotting paper through the jelly so the fat adheres to it, beat a whole egg in a casserole and pour the jelly slowly into it
Set over fire and stir constantly with a new cooking spoon until it boils, then remove it, pour into a felt hat
Place the trout on a large plate, pour some of the clear jelly over it, let it stand and color part of the jelly green
Take fat clove leaves, pound them in a mortar, press the juice through a cloth and make the jelly green with it
When the jelly is half set, pour the green jelly over the trout, let it set completely and pour clear jelly over once more
Garnish the fish to taste

title: Forellen mit saurer Sulz (Trout in Sour Jelly) - Variant

steps: Boil the trout blue and place on a dish, cover tightly so the blue does not disappear
Make the following sauce: Chop 2 cleaned calf's feet together with 1 Loth isinglass, add fish stock so it makes 1-1.5 Maas
Cook for 2 to 3 hours, strain the jelly through a fine sieve and let it stand in a bowl for a quarter hour so the sediment remains on the bottom
Draw a sheet of blotting paper through the jelly so the fat adheres to it, beat a whole egg in a casserole and pour the jelly slowly into it
Set over fire and stir constantly with a new cooking spoon until it boils, then remove it and pour into a felt hat
Place the trout on a large plate, pour some of the clear jelly over it and let it stand
Color part of the jelly green in a dish: take fat clove leaves, pound them in a mortar, press the juice through a cloth and make the jelly green with it
When it is half set, pour the green jelly over the trout, let it set completely and pour clear jelly over once more
The fish can now be garnished to taste

Cut in 10 loths of butter

Add one quarter pound of clean small raisins, 2 loths of large pitted raisins cut in half, one loth of ground sugar, one knife point of salt, 4 blanched bitter almonds coarsely ground, and 4 whole eggs

title: Frankfurter Speise (Frankfurt Dish)
description: Prepared with apples, white wine, and egg yolks.
steps: Steam 16 to 18 peeled Borsdorf apples, from which the core has been removed, in a casserolle with 4 loth sugar and 1 schoppen white wine
Make a crème with Maraschino as follows: let 3 schoppen milk, 4 loth sugar and 1 piece cinnamon cook together for a time
Smooth 8 egg yolks and 1 cooking spoon flour together, pour the boiling milk over it along with 1/2 glass Maraschino
Let everything come to the boil once more in the pan, spurt it vigorously in a pot
Place the apples on a plate, make a firm water pastry dough and make a ring of it around the plate
Brush with an egg, pour the crème over the apples and let them bake golden in a baking oven

title: Frankfurter Wildbretpastete (Frankfurt Venison Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with roe, bacon, and onions.

ingredients.name: thick muscles of a roe deer leg
ingredients.sourceText: thick muscles of a roe deer leg

steps: Make beautiful pieces from the thick muscles of a roe deer leg.
Beat them and lard them with bacon.
Braise them in a covered saucepan with finely cut onions, bay leaves, pepper, and salt.
When the meat is golden, let it cool on a plate.
Skin the remaining meat from the roe deer leg and pound it with {{source-6}}, half pound tender veal, half pound lean bacon, 2 cleaned herrings, and the yellow of 1 lemon into a dough.
Add 4 shallot onions and 2 ordinary chopped and braised onions.
Soak 1 peeled cross roll, press it out, and add it along with salt and all kinds of fine spices to the meat.
Rub everything together on a grater to a foam.
Mix 2 eggs, 2 spoonfuls chopped capers, 12 peeled olives, and quarter pound cleaned truffles cut into pieces.

title: Französische Jussuppe (French Meat Broth Soup)
description: A soup made with meat, butter or fat, and onions.
steps: Put a piece of butter or fat in a casserole
Line the bottom with onions, yellow turnips and celery
Cut 2 pounds of beef into small pieces and place in the casserole
Add any leftover bones if available
Cover the casserole and let it steam for one hour
Uncover and let the steamed mixture brown well
When it is brown, add a ladle full of water
Fill the casserole with meat broth and let it cook 2 hours
Cut slices from black bread and add to the casserole
After everything has cooked together for half an hour, pass it through a hair sieve
Let it come to a boil once more in the casserole and serve
If desired, eggs can be beaten into the soup bowl

title: Frische Heringe zu Braten (Fresh Herrings for Frying)
description: Prepared with herrings, fat, and vinegar.
steps: Scale the herrings, gut them, wash them, make a few light cuts along the back and salt them for 1/2 hour.
Dry them off and roll them evenly in flour mixed with pepper and salt.
Fry or bake the herrings in steaming fat until cooked through and golden.
Once cooled, pour over the herrings a sauce made from vinegar, water, salt, spices and onion slices that has been brought to a boil, seasoned to taste, then cooled.
Pack them in a stone pot, tie it shut, and use as needed.
Note: herrings should only be purchased when the head looks entirely pale; once it has turned red, the herrings are not fresh. The fat should be clarified.

title: Fruchtsauce (Fruit Sauce)
description: A fruit sauce using currants, blueberries or fruit juice, with orange peel and sugar.

ingredients.name: Johannisbeeren oder Blaubeeren, oder 1/2 l beliebiger auch gemischter Fruchtsaft
ingredients.sourceText: 250 g Johannisbeeren oder Blaubeeren, oder 1/2 l beliebiger auch gemischter Fruchtsaft

steps: Die abgebeerten Beeren werden gewaschen und mit Apfelsinenschale und Wasser auf den Herd gestellt; das Staerkemehl wird mit Wasser ausgeloest.

Die Beeren werden zerkocht, durch ein Sieb gestrichen und mit Zucker abgeschmeckt. Der Saft wird wieder in den Topf zurueckgegossen, mit dem in Wasser geloesten Staerkemehl aufgekocht, in einen Napf gegossen und kaltgestellt. Wird Fruchtsaft verwendet, so kann der Zucker fehlen, die Sauce stellt sich dann aber meistens teurer. Man gibt die Sauce zu gelben oben weissen Flammeris oder Puddings und auch zu Mehl- oder Griesskloessen.

Es koennen auch Pflaumen (Pflaumensauce) oder Kirschen (Kirschsauce) oder Fruchtsuppenreste verwendet werden. Pflaumenmus in derselben Weise verduennt ergibt Pflaumenmussauce, Kirschmus: Kirschsauce. Man kann die Fruchtfluessigkeit nach Geschmack beliebig verduennen und kalt als Fruchtkaltschale geben oder auch mit 30 g Staerkemehl verkocht zu Fruchtflammerl benutzen.
Die durchgestrichenen Reste kann man noch einmal etwas mit aufkochen, durchgiessen und zur Sauce mit verwenden.

Place the liver on the serving platter.
Strain the sauce through a fine sieve and pour over.
Sprinkle some chopped lemon zest on top.

title: Gebackene Aepfelschnitten (Fried Apple Slices)
description: Prepared with bread, wine, and apples.
steps: Cut off the hard rind from the bottom of 3 to 5 pieces of Mundbroden
Dip 3 to 4 slices at a time in milk, lay them on top of each other, and continue until all are used
Make a thin dough (Flädchenteig) from 1 schoppen lukewarm wine and flour
Peel 6 to 8 apples, put a piece of butter in a casserole with the apples, 2 loth sugar, and {{source-7}}
Cook them soft, add 2 knife points of cinnamon, stir all together like a porridge, and let it cool on a plate
Heat lard, take half a spoonful of the apple mixture and stir it into the dough
Take 2 of the bread slices, spread a tablespoonful of the cooked apples on one, cover with another slice, dip in the dough
Fry until golden and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon

title: Gebackene Chokoladecrême (Baked Chocolate Cream)
description: Prepared with chocolate, egg yolks, and egg whites.
steps: Dissolve a quarter pound chocolate in a brass pan with one glass of water
Cook it with one maas milk, 4 loth sugar and a knife point of cinnamon
Stir 8 egg yolks smooth with half a cooking spoon of flour and cold milk
Stir the chocolate to it
Let everything draw once more in the pan together
Spoon it into a pot until it cools slightly
Pour the cream through a hair sieve onto the plate
Whip a stiff foam from the 8 egg whites
Cover the entire cream with it
Decorate with 2 loth almonds finely cut lengthwise
Sprinkle green granulated sugar over it
Place the cream in the roasting oven a quarter hour before serving so it becomes hot again

title: Gebackene Flädlein mit Mandelfülle (Fried Pancakes with Almond Filling)
description: Prepared with milk or water, blanched almonds, and lemon.

ingredients.name: blanched almonds, finely pounded with egg white
ingredients.sourceText: 1/4 pound blanched almonds, finely pounded with egg white

steps: Prepare pancakes (Flädlein) as usual, but add some sugar to the batter
Mix 1/4 pound blanched almonds with egg white and pound finely
Beat together with 6 loth finely pounded sugar, 1/2 lemon zest, and 3 whole eggs until thick
Separate the pancakes and spread the filling on each one
Roll them together
Cut each roll in half
Turn in beaten egg
Fry well in lard
Make a wine or milk sauce with arak to serve alongside

title: Gebackene Kalbsfüße (Fried Calf's Feet)
description: Prepared with calf's feet, salt, and water.
steps: Remove the skin from the feet
Cook them soft in salt water

Dip the pieces one after another into the batter
Fry them golden brown

title: Gebackene Küchlein von Kalbsbrieschen (Fried Cakes of Calf's Sweetbreads)
description: A cake made with sweetbreads, rolls, and shallot.
steps: Soak 2 grated rolls in water and press out firmly
Stir {{source-2}} lightly in a bowl and add the rolls
Simmer 2 calf's sweetbreads in water
Cut them, after removing the windpipes and veins, into small pieces
Braise in a casserole with a piece of butter 2 to 3 chopped shallot onions, some chives or parsley, and the sweetbreads
Let cool, then stir in 5 eggs one after another into the butter-stirred rolls
Add the sweetbreads along with salt and nutmeg
Form round cakes from the mixture
Fry beautifully golden in lard
Can be served as a side dish

title: Gebackene Mandeln (Fried Almond Cakes)
description: A cake made with egg yolks, lemon, and lard.
steps: 3 Eidotter und 1 Ei an ein Viertelpfund Zucker rühren.
In eine Schüssel nehmen.
Eine Citrone am Reibeisen abreiben und dazugeben.
Welschnußgroße Butter zergehen lassen und alles untereinander rühren.
5 Loth Mehl darunter mischen.
Teig auf dem Nudelbrett fingersdick auswalken.
Mit einem blechernen Mödelchen in Mandelform ausstechen.
Die Küchelchen im heißen Schmalz gelb ausbacken.
Mit Zucker bestreuen.
Beim Ausstechen nicht zu viel Mehl hineinarbeiten.

title: Gebackene Mandeln anderer Art (Fried Almond Cakes, Another Way)
description: Almond cakes made with eggs, rose water and lemon, flavored with cinnamon.
steps: Ein Viertelpfund abgezogene Mandeln mit Rosenwasser ganz fein stoßen.
In eine Schüssel bringen.
2 Eier darunter schlagen.
4 Loth fein gestoßenen Zucker hinzufügen.
Die Masse eine Viertelstunde lang rühren.
Die am Reibeisen abgeriebene Schale einer halben Citrone und eine Messerspitze voll Zimmt dazugeben.
Mit 12 Loth feinem Mehl gut rühren.
Auf einem mit Mehl bestreuten Brett kleinf ingerdick auswalken.
Mit einem Mödelchen Mandeln ausstechen.
Im heißen Schmalz schön gelb ausbacken.
Mit Zucker bestreuen.

title: Gebackene Milch (Baked Milk)
description: Prepared with milk, egg yolks, and lemon.
steps: Stir together 5 whole eggs, 5 egg yolks, and 1/2 measures milk well
Take sugar on which a lemon has been grated
Roast 3 spoonfuls flour in hot lard until light yellow
Pour the milk with the eggs to it
Cook everything until it becomes thick, stirring constantly
Should the lard cook out, it must be skimmed off
When the porridge is on the plate, sprinkle sugar and cinnamon on it

title: Gebackene Vanillecrême (Baked Vanilla Cream)
description: Prepared with vanilla, egg yolks, and egg whites.
steps: Cook 1 finger-length vanilla piece with 1 schoppen milk for a quarter hour
In a brass pan, stir 4 spoonfuls flour smooth with cold milk
Add 4 loth sugar, 6 egg yolks and 1 more schoppen milk, as well as the vanilla milk

Slowly fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites
Butter a dish, fill with the cream and bake until golden yellow

title: Gebackene Weincrême (Baked Wine Cream)
description: Prepared with wine, egg yolks, and egg whites.
steps: Let half a maas wine cook with the peel of a lemon, one piece whole cinnamon, and a quarter pound sugar
Stir a little flour smooth with cold water, beat 8 egg yolks into it
Stir this into the boiling wine and let everything cook once more in the pan
Pour the cream through a fine sieve onto the plate
Beat the 8 egg whites into snow and form round balls the size of a hen's egg
Sprinkle them with finely cut almonds and coarsely pounded sugar
Place the cream in the oven for a quarter hour before serving

title: Gebratene Ochsenzunge (Braised Ox Tongue)
description: Prepared with ox tongue, onions, and lemons.
steps: Clean an ox tongue and simmer it until the skin can be removed
Lard it
Place it in a casserole
Add onions, lemons, bay leaves, salt, pepper and mace
Add 6 loth butter and a glass of wine
Cover the casserole
Let it braise
You can also braise this tongue in the oven or on a spit
When serving add lemons

title: Gebratene Schnepfe (Roasted Woodcock)
description: Prepared with woodcock, onion, and bread.
steps: Pluck the woodcock with its head, though it is better if the head is not marinated.
Turn the feet back onto the thighs and remove the entrails.
Rub the bird well with salt, pepper, and some cloves.
Place an onion and a piece of black bread inside it, tuck the head onto the breast, and press out the eyes.
Roast it in a casserole with a piece of fat.
Lay onions, yellow carrots, and parsnip roots beside it, covering the casserole so the bird stays white.
Pour a little jus over it.
For the woodcock farce: Take the giblets (but not the stomach), clean the intestines, and mince them very finely with the shell of half a lemon, parsley, and the liver of a young hen.
Add nutmeg, white pepper, and 3 finger-widths of flour.
In a small casserole, stir together in melted butter 2 tablespoonfuls of flour, some red wine, and a spoonful of the fat the woodcocks were roasted in, but do not cook it.
Cut white bread without crust into slices, fry them in lard, spread the woodcock farce on them, and place the slices on the platter.
Put the woodcocks in the center, garnish with parsley and lemon, and serve the sauce separately.

title: Gebratener Auerhahn (Roasted Capercaillie)
description: Prepared with onion, lemon, and bay leaf.

ingredients.name: Pork skin (from half the side of a young pig)
ingredients.sourceText: Pork skin (from half the side of a young pig)

steps: The bird can be kept dead for 6 days; pluck it, singe it, and clean it carefully with a cloth without washing if possible
Remove the entrails carefully so the gall is not crushed
Rub it with salt, pepper, cloves, and mace
Cut into the breastbone and remove the claws but leave the feet on the body
Dress it nicely and fill it with an onion, half a lemon, a bay leaf, and a piece of butter
Bind it firmly together and cut off the head and neck so the skin remains on the body
Wrap it in the skin of half the side of a young pig and sew it firmly with a strong trussing needle
Roast it slowly and yellowly in the oven; if young it takes 2 hours, if old 3 hours
Pour a Schoppen of wine over it and baste it frequently
Serve it with the skin and garnish with parsley and lemon
Treat the sauce as for roasted turkey
